title: The Window Fitting
light: A big sash window behind them, soft daylight wrapping both outlines. I exposed for skin and let the glass go white.
composition: Two profiles face each other across the frame. The bright glass behind keeps both outlines clean and separate.
lens: Try 50mm at f/2 from across the room, level with her waist so the window frame stays straight.
moment: The flower girl looks up and laughs mid fitting. I give the bride a small job with her hands and wait for the look up.
before_shoot: Clear the sill and the floor of bags and bottles. In a backlit frame every bit of clutter turns into a silhouette.

directions.label: FACE TO FACE
directions.say: Stand side on to the window and face each other, nice and close.

directions.label: A SMALL JOB
directions.say: Take her hands and fix her bracelet for her. No rush at all.

directions.label: THE SECRET
directions.say: Tell her a secret about today. Something only you two know.

title: The Doorway Reveal
light: Even window light bouncing around white walls. Nothing harsh, so every face at the door reads clearly.
composition: Bride soft in the near left, friends sharp in the far doorway. The open door frames them and the floor leads in.
lens: Try 35mm at f/2.8 over the bride's shoulder, focus locked on the doorway before anyone walks in.
moment: Her friends see the dress for the first time. Hands to mouths, one arm on the door. I keep them outside until she is ready.
before_shoot: Pre-focus on the doorway and agree a knock signal. You get one take at this reaction, so be set before it happens.

directions.label: HOLD THE HALL
directions.say: Wait in the hall until I knock. Then come in together.

directions.label: DON'T TURN
directions.say: Stay facing the mirror. Don't turn around until you hear them.

directions.label: JUST REACT
directions.say: Okay, open the door and walk in. Don't pose. Just react.

title: The Double Door Reveal
light: A dark corridor behind him, a bright room in front. He steps out of shadow into soft window light.
composition: The double doors make a frame inside the frame. Her veil fills the right third out of focus.
lens: Try 50mm at f/2 from behind her shoulder. Keep the doors square to the sensor.
moment: Both doors open at once and his face does the rest. I have him rest his hands on the handles and wait for my nod.
before_shoot: Test both doors before the reveal. A sticky latch or a squeak will kill the moment.

directions.label: HANDS READY
directions.say: Hands on both handles. Wait for my nod before you open.

directions.label: TURN A LITTLE
directions.say: Turn your shoulders just slightly toward the window for me.

directions.label: OPEN UP
directions.say: Now open them both together and take her in.

title: The Quiet Room
light: Flat window light from camera left fills the room. The veil catches it and glows against the dark headboard.
composition: Wide and level. She sits low on the bed, legs long to the right. The shoes and one glass tell the rest.
lens: Try 28mm to 35mm from the corner of the room, camera at chest height, verticals straight.
moment: A pause before the dress. She looks toward the window and lets the veil settle. I just ask her to breathe.
before_shoot: Strip the room first. Hide the tags, chargers and coffee cups. Leave one glass and the shoes.

directions.label: SIT LONG
directions.say: Sit right on the edge of the bed and stretch your legs out long.

directions.label: VEIL DOWN
directions.say: Let the veil fall over your face. Hands relaxed on the sheet.

directions.label: LOOK AWAY
directions.say: Look out the window and think about the next hour.

title: The Bath Toast
light: Bright daylight bouncing off white walls and tiles. Clean and punchy, and kind to a black suit.
composition: Low and wide. The checked tiles lead to him, the door sits behind his head and the tap guards the right edge.
lens: Try 24mm to 28mm close to the floor. Keep him away from the frame edge so he doesn't stretch.
moment: A quiet toast before he leaves. I hand him the glass and ask him to sit like he owns the place.
before_shoot: Bathrooms are small and full of mirrors. Check every angle so you aren't in your own shot.

directions.label: TAKE A SEAT
directions.say: Sit on the edge of the bath. One foot forward.

directions.label: LEAN BACK
directions.say: Free hand on your knee. Lean back a little.

directions.label: THE TOAST
directions.say: Glass up. That one's for you, mate. Take a sip.

title: The Room Embrace
light: Soft daylight from the window behind the bed. Low contrast, so the emotion carries the frame.
composition: A landscape frame with the embrace on the right two thirds. The bed and lamp sit soft on the left.
lens: Try 50mm at f/1.8 a few metres back. Close enough to feel it, far enough not to intrude.
moment: A hug that lasts longer than planned. She closes her eyes. I stay quiet and keep shooting through it.
before_shoot: Know who is coming into the room and when. These hugs happen once and they happen fast.

directions.label: COME IN
directions.say: Come in whenever you're ready. I'll stay out of the way.

directions.label: HOLD ON
directions.say: Hold on a bit longer. There's no need to let go.

directions.label: ONE THING
directions.say: Before you step back, tell each other one thing.

title: The Buttonhole Lay
light: Soft open shade with no hard shadow. The blue board and ribbons stay cool and even.
composition: Straight down. Eight stems scattered at loose angles, with space around each one.
lens: Try 50mm or a 100mm macro, standing over the board with the sensor dead flat.
moment: Detail time while the groomsmen dress. I lay them out at odd angles so the set looks scattered, not lined up.
before_shoot: Bring your own board in a colour that suits the palette. Brush any pollen off the petals first.

directions.label: ONE AT A TIME
directions.say: Can you pass me the buttonholes one at a time, please?

directions.label: TURN IT
directions.say: Turn that one so the ribbon faces out.

directions.label: HANDS OFF
directions.say: Perfect. Nobody touch them for one minute.

title: The Seated Veil
light: Hard side light from a window at camera left cuts across her face and leg. Everything outside the beam falls to black.
composition: She fills the frame. The lace train spills across the bottom and the veil arcs away to the right.
lens: Try 35mm to 50mm, standing slightly above her so the train fills the lower half.
moment: A held stare, not a smile. I turn her into the light, then ask for stillness and eye contact.
before_shoot: Find the one shaft of light first, then bring her to it. Underexpose so the shadows stay deep.

directions.label: SIT BACK
directions.say: Sit back on the chaise and pull one knee up toward you.

directions.label: FIND THE LIGHT
directions.say: Hand on your ankle. Chin toward the window.

directions.label: THE STARE
directions.say: Now eyes to me. Don't smile. Just hold it.

title: The Veiled Corner
light: Soft window light from the left. The veil diffuses it a second time, so skin turns smooth and low contrast.
composition: Tucked into a corner, the walls make a triangle behind her. The veil makes a second one from head to floor.
lens: Try 50mm to 85mm at f/2, just above her eye line.
moment: A quiet, dreamy pause. I drape the veil over her, then ask her to lean on her hand and look past me.
before_shoot: Steam the veil edge. Every crease shows the moment light comes through it.

directions.label: SIT FORWARD
directions.say: Sit forward on the stool, elbow on your knee.

directions.label: SOFT HAND
directions.say: Chin into your hand. Lighter, like you're thinking.

directions.label: DRIFT OFF
directions.say: Look just past my shoulder and let your mind wander.

title: The Lace in the Dark
light: Directional window light from camera right rakes across the lace, so each flower stands out against a dark room.
composition: Three quarter length with her profile on the right. The veil runs a long diagonal from top right to bottom left.
lens: Try 85mm at f/2.8 so the background falls away and the lace stays sharp.
moment: Hands folded, eyes down. I lift the veil out to the side, let it fall, then ask her to look to the floor.
before_shoot: Turn the room lights off. Mixed light turns white lace grey.

directions.label: SIDE ON
directions.say: Turn your shoulder to the window and fold your hands low.

directions.label: EYES DOWN
directions.say: Drop your chin and look down toward the floor.

directions.label: SETTLE
directions.say: Long breath out. Let your shoulders sink.

title: The Floral Veil Glance
light: Soft open shade between two columns. Even light lets the floral appliqué read across her back.
composition: Back to camera, face turned over the shoulder. The pillars frame her on both sides.
lens: Try 85mm at f/2. The compression keeps the columns soft behind her.
moment: The look back. I ask her to walk away from me, stop, and look over her shoulder.
before_shoot: Spread the veil evenly across her back so the appliqué pattern isn't bunched.

directions.label: WALK AWAY
directions.say: Walk away from me, slowly, toward the wall.

directions.label: DROP A SHOULDER
directions.say: Stop there. Drop your shoulder toward me.

directions.label: JUST YOUR EYES
directions.say: Now just your eyes back to me. Keep your chin down.

title: The Window Train
light: Backlight from one tall window. The veil turns translucent and the room around it goes black.
composition: A narrow column of light on the left. The veil fans from her toward the lens and fills the bottom.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm low to the floor, so the veil runs toward you.
moment: Total stillness. I spread the veil, step back, and ask her to look out the window and not move.
before_shoot: Expose for the window, not the room. Check your highlights before she gets into place.

directions.label: IN THE WINDOW
directions.say: Stand in the window, side on, and look out.

directions.label: STAY STILL
directions.say: Stay right there. I'm going to fan out your veil.

directions.label: CHIN UP
directions.say: Lift your chin a touch. Hold that for me.

title: The Curtain Light
light: Sun through sheer curtains. It softens on her face and throws bright shapes across the fabric.
composition: She stands in the left third. A curtain blows across the right side as a soft foreground layer.
lens: Try 35mm to 50mm and shoot through the edge of the curtain.
moment: Fabric moving around a still subject. I have someone lift the curtain and let it drop between frames.
before_shoot: Bring a helper to work the curtain and shoot in bursts. The fabric never falls the same way twice.

directions.label: HOLD THE EDGE
directions.say: Hold the curtain edge lightly in one hand.

directions.label: LOOK DOWN
directions.say: Look down toward the floor, chin over your shoulder.

directions.label: LET IT FALL
directions.say: Lift the curtain and let it drop. Once more.

title: The Stair Shadow
light: Hard sun on a white wall. The shadow shapes are as much the subject as she is.
composition: Curved steps lead from the bottom left up to her. The lantern balances the top and the shadow fills the left.
lens: Try 35mm from the foot of the stairs, so the curves stay in frame.
moment: Lifting the gown to climb. I ask her to gather the skirt, step up, then pause halfway.
before_shoot: Hard light moves fast. Work out where the shadow will fall ten minutes from now.

directions.label: GATHER UP
directions.say: Gather your skirt in both hands.

directions.label: HALFWAY
directions.say: Step up and pause halfway.

directions.label: KEEP CLIMBING
directions.say: Look down at your feet. Keep walking slowly.

title: The Sofa Window
light: Window light from the right, slightly hard. It sculpts her cheekbone and leaves the far side of the room dark.
composition: Tight and diagonal. Her shoulders run across the frame and the sofa cushion leads up to her face.
lens: Try 50mm to 85mm at f/2 from a seated height.
moment: A breath between events. I hand her the glass and ask her to turn her face to the light and forget I'm there.
before_shoot: Turn her until the window shows as a catchlight in both eyes.

directions.label: SINK IN
directions.say: Sit into the corner of the sofa, arm along the cushion.

directions.label: GLASS LOW
directions.say: Hold the glass low, in both hands.

directions.label: FAR AWAY
directions.say: Turn to the window and look at the farthest building.

title: The Column Lean
light: Open shade under a colonnade. The stone behind falls dark while her lace and veil carry the light.
composition: The column runs top to bottom right of centre. She leans into it and a branch of leaves frames the top right corner.
lens: Try 50mm at f/2. Step back until the column fills the height of the frame.
moment: Veil down, eyes closed, a soft lean. I ask her to rest her weight on the column and close her eyes.
before_shoot: Check the column for dust and flaking paint. White lace marks easily.

directions.label: LEAN IN
directions.say: Lean your shoulder into the column. Let it take your weight.

directions.label: HOLD THE VEIL
directions.say: Hold the veil lightly at your waist.

directions.label: REMEMBER
directions.say: Close your eyes and smile like you just remembered something.

title: The Window Hall
light: Arched windows straight behind them. Strong backlight rims both figures and throws long shadows over the boards.
composition: Small figures in a big room. They stand between two arches and the floorboards lead up to their feet.
lens: Try 35mm from the middle of the room, camera at waist height.
moment: A held look across joined hands. I bring them to the light, join their hands and ask them to talk quietly.
before_shoot: Expose for the windows and lift the shadows later. Watch for flare across the lens.

directions.label: BETWEEN THE ARCHES
directions.say: Stand facing each other, right between those two windows.

directions.label: HANDS LOW
directions.say: Hold both hands, low between you.

directions.label: TONIGHT
directions.say: Tell each other what you're most excited about tonight.

title: The Garden from Above
light: Bright afternoon sun with dappled shade on the paving. Her dress catches the sun while he stands in shadow.
composition: Shot from above. The veil sweeps in a curve toward him and he anchors the bottom of the frame.
lens: Try 35mm from a balcony or upper step, looking down over the garden.
moment: She walks a slow loop and the veil follows her. He stays still and watches.
before_shoot: Find your high spot before the couple arrives. Lay the veil out flat so it lands in a clean curve.

directions.label: STAND STILL
directions.say: Stand right here and don't move.

directions.label: SLOW LOOP
directions.say: Walk slowly around him in a big circle.

directions.label: TURN BACK
directions.say: When you reach the railing, turn back to him.

title: The City Walk
light: Bright overcast city light. It bounces off pale stone and keeps the white dress full of detail.
composition: Shot from behind as they walk. The building edge leads into the distance and her train fills the bottom right.
lens: Try 35mm to 50mm, walking behind them at their pace.
moment: A laugh over the shoulder. I ask them to walk, and her to look back at me after a few steps.
before_shoot: Walk the route once without the couple. Check for traffic, bins and signage in the background.

directions.label: WALK AWAY
directions.say: Hold hands and walk away from me, nice and slow.

directions.label: SWING
directions.say: Swing your hands a little as you go.

directions.label: LOOK BACK
directions.say: Now look back at me. Tell him what I just said.

title: The Shadow Hold
light: Hard, low sun. It throws long, crisp shadows across bright pavement.
composition: No people, only shadows. Their arms and joined hands cut a zigzag across plain concrete.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm, pointing down at the ground.
moment: Their shadows reach for each other. I ask them to stand apart and stretch until their hands meet.
before_shoot: Keep your own shadow out of frame. Move until the sun throws it behind you.

directions.label: STEP APART
directions.say: Stand a big step apart, facing each other.

directions.label: FINGERTIPS
directions.say: Reach out and just touch fingertips.

directions.label: STRETCH
directions.say: Lean back a little. Let your arms stretch out.

title: The Grand Stair
light: Soft skylight from above. It lights the wall and the rail while the lower stairwell falls darker.
composition: Strong diagonals. The banisters run corner to corner and the couple sit high where the lines meet.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm from the landing below, tilted up.
moment: A kiss on the stairs. I place them a few steps apart, then ask him to step down to her.
before_shoot: Clear the stairs of guests and staff. One stray figure on a staircase breaks the lines.

directions.label: TWO STEPS
directions.say: Stand a couple of steps apart on the stairs.

directions.label: STEP DOWN
directions.say: Step down to her. Hand on her waist.

directions.label: THE KISS
directions.say: Now kiss her. Slowly.

title: The Close Dance
light: Soft open shade, with warm stone bouncing light back into their faces.
composition: Tight. Faces fill the top, joined hands sit in the centre and her lace sleeve leads in from the bottom right.
lens: Try 85mm at f/2 from a few metres away.
moment: A slow dance with no music. I ask them to hold hands like a waltz and sway.
before_shoot: Check the ring hand faces the camera. It's a small detail, but every couple notices.

directions.label: HAND UP
directions.say: Take her hand up to your chest.

directions.label: CHEEK IN
directions.say: Rest your forehead on his cheek.

directions.label: SWAY
directions.say: Now sway. Tell him something that makes him grin.

title: The Navy Door Kiss
light: Open shade in a deep doorway. Even light holds the white dress against the dark navy door.
composition: Symmetrical. The door sits dead centre between two columns and her veil sweeps across the steps.
lens: Try 35mm, square on to the door, verticals straight.
moment: Her arm around his neck, the veil lifting. I wait for a breeze, or have someone throw the veil.
before_shoot: Look for a door with a strong colour and clean steps. Sweep the leaves before you shoot.

directions.label: AT THE DOOR
directions.say: Stand in front of the door, close together.

directions.label: PULL HIM IN
directions.say: Arm around his neck. Pull him in.

directions.label: ON THREE
directions.say: Throw the veil on three. One, two, three.

title: The Column Steps
light: Overcast daylight between tall columns. Soft and even, so the lace detail holds.
composition: Two levels. He stands higher on the left, she stands front and right, and her train fills the bottom.
lens: Try 35mm from the bottom step, slightly below her eye line.
moment: Two separate poses in one frame. I give each a job. He does his button, she looks up to the light.
before_shoot: Spread the train wide over the steps. On a big set of stairs it reads as scale.

directions.label: UP A STEP
directions.say: Up one step for me. Do your top button.

directions.label: CHIN UP
directions.say: Hands by your sides, chin up.

directions.label: TO THE LIGHT
directions.say: Both of you, look toward the light. Hold.

title: The Balcony Arches
light: Soft skylight fills a white room. Very high key, with almost no shadow.
composition: The architecture is the frame. Arches and a balustrade fill the page and the couple sit small in the lower centre.
lens: Try 35mm to 50mm from a balcony on the far side of the atrium.
moment: He leads her along the balcony. I direct from across the room, so we agree hand signals first.
before_shoot: Agree hand signals before you split up. Shouting across a foyer ruins the mood.

directions.label: THE MIDDLE
directions.say: Walk to the middle of the balcony and stop.

directions.label: BEHIND HIM
directions.say: Hold his hand and step in behind him.

directions.label: LEAD HER
directions.say: Now walk her along. Nice and slow.

title: The Back Seat
light: Daylight through the car windows. Soft, flat and kind to skin.
composition: Tight and layered. He sits soft in the foreground, she looks out the window and the car frame boxes them in.
lens: Try 35mm from the opposite seat or through the open door.
moment: The ride between ceremony and reception. Neither looks at the camera. I ask them to settle in and talk.
before_shoot: Ask the driver for two minutes parked before you leave. Shooting a moving car is a gamble.

directions.label: SLIDE IN
directions.say: Slide right in close to each other.

directions.label: LOOK OUT
directions.say: Look out your windows for a second.

directions.label: FAVOURITE PART
directions.say: Now tell her your favourite part so far.

title: The Garden Stairs
light: Open shade with sun high in the trees. Even light across every face.
composition: Built on the stairs with heads at different heights. The couple sit centre and friends spill up and down the steps.
lens: Try 35mm from the bottom step, slightly below eye level.
moment: A styled group with personality. I place the couple first, then give each friend a different pose.
before_shoot: Plan the arrangement before everyone arrives. Big groups lose energy fast.

directions.label: COUPLE FIRST
directions.say: Couple, middle of the stairs. Everyone else build around you.

directions.label: MIX IT UP
directions.say: Every second person, take a seat on a step.

directions.label: OWN IT
directions.say: Look at me like you all own the place.

title: The Stone Arch
light: Soft open shade at a stone arch. The dark arch behind separates every head.
composition: Couple centred under the arch. The party fans out on both sides, some leaning, some seated on the step.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm close in, so the arch curves over the whole group.
moment: Relaxed and confident. I give each person somewhere to lean or sit, so nobody stands stiff.
before_shoot: Spread the train and veil across the bricks before the group steps in around it.

directions.label: FIND A WALL
directions.say: Couple under the arch. Everyone else, lean on the walls.

directions.label: HANDS
directions.say: Groomsmen, one hand in your pocket.

directions.label: EYES UP
directions.say: Everyone, chin down and eyes up to me.

title: The Party Cheer
light: Bright overcast sky. Flat light, so every face reads evenly at every height.
composition: A tight cluster from a low angle. Bodies overlap and crouch, and bouquets and glasses break up the top edge.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm close in, crouching low.
moment: Pure noise. I count them in and ask for the loudest cheer of the day.
before_shoot: Turn every bottle and can so the label faces away from the lens.

directions.label: SQUEEZE IN
directions.say: Squeeze in tight. Taller ones at the back.

directions.label: GET LOW
directions.say: Front row, drop down low for me.

directions.label: ON THREE
directions.say: Glasses up. Loudest cheer on three. One, two, three.

title: The Ring of Trees
light: High sun, straight down. Shadows stay short so the shapes on the ground read clearly.
composition: Perfect symmetry. A round drive circles a ring of trees, and the long table runs through the middle.
lens: A drone at roughly 60 metres, camera pointing straight down.
moment: The setting before anyone sits. I fly it once the tables are set and the guests are still elsewhere.
before_shoot: Check the airspace rules and the venue's drone policy. Charge two batteries.

directions.label: HOLD THE GUESTS
directions.say: Can we keep everyone out of the garden for five minutes?

directions.label: WATCH ABOVE
directions.say: Call out if anyone walks under the drone.

directions.label: TABLE LIGHTS
directions.say: Can we switch the table lights on while I'm up?

title: The Red Brick Quad
light: Bright sun from the side picks out the roof tiles and throws shadows from the battlements.
composition: An oblique drone angle. The building wraps the courtyard and two vintage cars on the drive add scale.
lens: A drone at about 40 metres, camera tilted down around 45 degrees.
moment: Arrival. The cars are parked and the tables are set. The whole day sits in one frame.
before_shoot: Fly it before the guests spill out. An empty courtyard reads cleaner from the air.

directions.label: PARK UP
directions.say: Can you leave the cars on the drive for ten minutes?

directions.label: CLEAR IT
directions.say: Tell me when the courtyard is clear.

directions.label: GOING UP
directions.say: Drone's going up now. Two minutes and I'm done.

title: The Cathedral Courtyard
light: Bright overcast. Even light, so the brick and slate texture holds across the whole building.
composition: Shot from a window above. The roof line runs left to right and the bell tower anchors the top left.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm from a high window. Keep the tower vertical.
moment: The building between moments. I grab it while everyone is still inside.
before_shoot: Ask the venue for upper floor access well before the day. Most will say yes if you ask early.

directions.label: ACCESS
directions.say: Is there a window upstairs I could use for one frame?

directions.label: HOLD THE DOOR
directions.say: Hold everyone at the door for one minute, please.

directions.label: RELEASE
directions.say: Thanks. Let them out now.

title: The Marquee at Blue Hour
light: Blue hour outside, warm lamps inside. The marquee glows against a deep sky.
composition: Low and wide. The lawn fills the bottom half and leads to the tent, its peaks against the clouds.
lens: Try 24mm on a tripod, far enough back to show the lawn.
moment: Dinner in full swing. The guests are small enough to read as warmth, not faces.
before_shoot: Bring a tripod and check the sunset time. The blue only lasts about twenty minutes.

directions.label: WALLS UP
directions.say: Can we keep the side walls rolled up for ten minutes?

directions.label: LIGHTS FULL
directions.say: Lights up full inside, please.

directions.label: SKY CHECK
directions.say: Call me the second the sky turns blue.

title: The Chapel Wall
light: Hard midday sun on pale stone. The sky deepens to blue and the trees throw shade at the edges.
composition: The building is the subject. The couple walk small along the bottom, with trees framing both sides.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm from across the lawn, verticals kept straight.
moment: A walk past the building. I send them from one tree to the other and shoot the whole way.
before_shoot: Step back until the spires sit inside the frame. Tilt up and the walls start to lean.

directions.label: TREE TO TREE
directions.say: Walk from that tree over to the other one.

directions.label: HOLD HANDS
directions.say: Hold hands, with the dress on the outside.

directions.label: HALFWAY
directions.say: Look at each other halfway along.

title: The Five Flutes
light: Soft, even light on a white backdrop. The glass edges go dark and the wine glows.
composition: Five flutes in a row with their mirror image below. Equal spacing, centred and calm.
lens: Try 50mm to 100mm, camera level with the base of the glasses.
moment: Before the toast. I line up the glasses myself while the room is still being set.
before_shoot: Polish every glass. A reflective surface doubles every smudge.

directions.label: BORROW
directions.say: Could I borrow five glasses and a pour, please?

directions.label: SAME LEVEL
directions.say: Same level in each one, if you can.

directions.label: RETURN
directions.say: Thank you. They'll be back in two minutes.

title: The Berry Cake
light: Hard light from the side lifts the berries and piped cream and leaves the background dark.
composition: Tight and diagonal. The cake runs off the top left and the tablecloth folds fill the bottom.
lens: Try 50mm to 85mm, close and slightly above the cake.
moment: The cake before the cut. I shoot it as soon as it's placed, while the fruit still shines.
before_shoot: Ask for the cake to be turned so its best side faces your light.

directions.label: A QUARTER TURN
directions.say: Can we turn the cake a quarter toward the window?

directions.label: TIDY THE CLOTH
directions.say: Pull that cloth tight across the front, please.

directions.label: ALL YOURS
directions.say: Perfect. One minute and it's all yours.

title: The Bow Coupe
light: Soft directional light on a dark backdrop. It lifts the cocktail, ring and ribbon off the background.
composition: The hand enters from the right. The glass sits high and the bow hangs down into empty space.
lens: Try 50mm to 85mm, close in.
moment: A hand holding the welcome drink. I tie the bow, then ask her to reach in from the side.
before_shoot: Bring a dark cloth or board. It turns any bar corner into a studio.

directions.label: BY THE STEM
directions.say: Hold the glass by the stem. Reach in from the side.

directions.label: SHOW THE RING
directions.say: Turn your ring toward me. Fingers soft.

directions.label: STILL
directions.say: Hold it still. Breathe out.

title: The Garden Plan
light: Soft late day light straight down. Gentle enough to keep the white tables from blowing out.
composition: A floor plan in a frame. Paths make a cross, round tables fill each quarter and the dance floor sits top left.
lens: A drone at about 50 metres, camera pointing straight down.
moment: Cocktail hour. Guests spread through the garden, small enough to read as pattern.
before_shoot: Fly before dark. A lit garden from the air at night loses all its detail.

directions.label: SPOTTER
directions.say: Keep an eye on the drone while I fly, please.

directions.label: CLEAR FLOOR
directions.say: Can we keep the dance floor clear for five minutes?

directions.label: TIME CHECK
directions.say: Call the time for me. We're done in five.

title: The Lawn Dance
light: Direct flash at night. It freezes them in white and drops the background to black.
composition: Two figures, full length. Arms reach toward each other and the dark lawn fills the bottom.
lens: Try 35mm at f/4 with on-camera flash, about four metres back.
moment: Shoes off and dancing on the grass. I take them outside after the speeches and ask them to forget I'm there.
before_shoot: Set the flash to manual and test on a stand-in. Grass eats light, so you'll need more power.

directions.label: SHOES OFF
directions.say: Out on the grass. Kick your shoes off.

directions.label: SPIN OUT
directions.say: Take her hand and spin her out.

directions.label: PULL IN
directions.say: Now pull her back in. Go.

title: The Cake Cut
light: Flash off to the side. It lights the cake and the couple and pushes the hedge behind them into shadow.
composition: Couple on the left, cake on the right, both the same height in frame. The tablecloth grounds the bottom.
lens: Try 35mm to 50mm at f/4, flash on a stand at 45 degrees.
moment: A nuzzle during the cut. I ask them to hold the knife together and look at each other, not me.
before_shoot: Ask the coordinator when the cut is. Be in position before the MC calls it.

directions.label: BOTH HANDS
directions.say: Both hands on the knife. Stand close.

directions.label: CHEEK TO CHEEK
directions.say: Cheek to cheek for me.

directions.label: IGNORE ME
directions.say: Ignore me. Look at each other and cut.

title: The Champagne Tower
light: Bounced flash lifts the couple out of a dim marquee. A slower shutter keeps the fairy lights glowing.
composition: Bride centre with her arm stretched to the bottle. The tower on the left catches the pour.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm close in, shutter around 1/30 to hold the fairy lights.
moment: The first pour. Champagne overflows and she reacts. I ask her to pour slowly so I get more than one frame.
before_shoot: Check the tower is stable and the floor is dry. Spilt champagne and long gowns don't mix.

directions.label: BOTTLE HIGH
directions.say: Bottle up high. Start pouring slowly.

directions.label: ARM AROUND
directions.say: Arm around her waist, and stay close.

directions.label: LET IT SPILL
directions.say: Keep pouring. Watch it spill over.

title: The Ballroom Spin
light: Off-camera light from behind rims them both and glows through her veil while the room stays dim.
composition: Couple in the lower centre on a patterned floor. Candles and tables sit behind and the ceiling fills the top.
lens: Try 24mm to 35mm wide, with a flash on a stand behind the couple.
moment: A spin during the first dance. I place the backlight before they walk onto the floor.
before_shoot: Hide the stand behind the groom. Check the frame with a test shot on a stand-in.

directions.label: CENTRE
directions.say: Start right in the middle of the floor.

directions.label: ARM OUT
directions.say: Arm out. Let him turn you.

directions.label: SPIN
directions.say: Spin out and laugh.
